findings.description: The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, meaning objects stored are not encrypted at rest by default, risking exposure of sensitive report data.

findings.issue_category: no bucket ACL / public access controls defined
findings.description: No ACL or public access block is defined for this bucket, leaving it potentially subject to default/public access settings and no explicit private restriction.
The bucket stores ledger export data but has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving sensitive financial data unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket despite storing model artifacts, exposing data to risk if bucket access controls fail.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so operational runbook data (potentially containing sensitive operational details) is stored unencrypted.

The ACL value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' is not a valid AWS canned ACL (the valid value for log delivery is 'log-delivery-write'); this typo could cause unexpected ACL application or apply failures, and if it resolves to an unintended permission it could grant broader write/read access than intended to the audit trail bucket.
force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its contents to be deleted without recovery, increasing risk of accidental or malicious data loss for archived reports.

findings.issue_category: unencrypted object upload / no server-side encryption specified
findings.description: The object is uploaded without specifying server-side encryption (kms_key_id or server_side_encryption), and the destination bucket also lacks encryption configuration, resulting in the vendor roster file being stored unencrypted in S3.
